brief.headline: New evening confusion reported Nov 15, after a Sep 23 fall and a Nov 5 ED visit for dehydration and dizziness, needs team follow-up on safety and workup results.

items.statement: On 2026-11-15 her son Marcus reported about two weeks of increased evening confusion, including once leaving the stove on. items.verifier_note: All details match the 2026-11-15 nursing note: two weeks of evening confusion, stove left on once, oriented to person and place but not date, no fever, and the planned urinalysis, medication review and PCP visit. The statement's note that no results are in the evidence is a valid observation.

items.statement: On 2026-09-23 she fell in the bathroom at night and was found on the floor by her son. She denied head strike and loss of consciousness, and no injury was noted. Fall risk was reassessed as high and a PT referral was placed.
items.verifier_note: The 2026-09-23 note supports every detail: bathroom fall at night, son found her, no head strike or loss of consciousness, no injury, fall risk reassessed as high, and a PT referral placed.

items.statement: The PT evaluation on 2026-10-01 found slow, unsteady gait with intermittent cane use and a Timed Up and Go of 19 seconds. items.verifier_note: The PT note supports the slow, unsteady gait with intermittent cane use, the TUG of 19 seconds, the walker, home safety evaluation and grab bar recommendations, and twice-weekly visits. The note contains nothing on whether the equipment is in place, so that remark is accurate.

items.statement: On 2026-11-05 she was seen in the partner hospital ED for dehydration and dizziness and released the same day, with no new medications. At PCP follow-up on 2026-11-11 she was back to baseline per her son, and the PCP planned close monitoring for two weeks.

What interim safety measures are in place for the stove and for evening supervision at home?

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and pull all encounters since the last IDT review: ED visits, urgent care, hospital admissions, observation stays, and any readmissions, with reasons and discharge summaries.

Falls and near-falls in the window: count, circumstances, injuries, and whether a post-fall review was completed. Note she is on antiplatelet and beta-blocker therapy, so check for any bleeding or bruising reported with falls.

Cardiac review (ischemic heart disease): chest pain or angina episodes, frequency of nitroglycerin spray use, dyspnea, palpitations, exercise tolerance, and any cardiology visits or testing ordered in the window.

Medication reconciliation: verify the active list against the prescriber record. Specifically reconcile the two simvastatin entries (10 mg started 2026-08-16 and 20 mg started 2020-07-11) to confirm whether this is an intended dose change, a duplicate, or an error, and confirm which one the patient is actually taking and who prescribed the change.

Medication adherence and tolerability: clopidogrel and metoprolol refill history, missed doses, held doses, and any side effects such as dizziness, fatigue, bradycardia-related symptoms, muscle aches, or GI bleeding signs. Check for any new medication starts or stops in the window beyond the simvastatin change.
Blood pressure and heart rate trend across the window (seated and standing if available), noting any hypotension, orthostatic symptoms, or resting heart rate below the team's documented threshold.

Weight and BMI trend (BMI 30+ on record): compare current weight with prior review and enrollment baseline, and note any unintended weight loss or gain over 5% in the window. Review nutrition intake and any dietitian referral status.
Glycemic status given prediabetes: review most recent HbA1c or fasting glucose, date of last lab, and whether repeat testing is due or overdue.
Lipid panel and statin follow-up: check whether a lipid panel was drawn after the simvastatin change and whether it is due per the care plan.
Oncology history (breast cancer, 1997): confirm surveillance schedule, any new breast symptoms, and whether oncology follow-up or screening items are current or overdue.

Function and ADLs/IADLs: changes in bathing, dressing, toileting, transfers, meal preparation, medication management, and transportation since last review, using the team's standard functional measure if one is in use.
Cognition and mood: any cognitive screen or observed change, delirium signs, depression screen score, social withdrawal, and attendance at PACE day programming and therapy sessions in the window.

Caregiver and social situation: any change in living arrangement, caregiver availability or strain, transportation barriers, housing or safety concerns, and advance directive or health-care proxy status.

Care-plan items due or overdue as of 2026-11-30: goals of care review, immunizations, preventive screenings, PACE assessment reassessment dates, and any open action items from the last IDT meeting. Summarize what changed and frame open questions for the team without making treatment recommendations.
Allergy record shows no entries; confirm with the patient and pharmacy that no allergies or adverse drug reactions have been newly reported.
